tasks.title: Fix 1/3: Pass `conversationId` and `leadId` to AIChatSidebar
tasks.description: Fix the disconnection between the UI and the conversation tracking system by adding the missing `conversationId` and `leadId` props to the AIChatSidebar component in ChatsPage.tsx.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually verify that the props are passed correctly using React Developer Tools. Check that the application does not crash and the sidebar still renders.

subtasks.title: Add `conversationId` Prop to AIChatSidebar Component
subtasks.description: Locate the `AIChatSidebar` component instantiation in `ChatsPage.tsx` and pass the `conversationId` from the `selectedChat` object as a prop.
subtasks.details: In `src/pages/ChatsPage.tsx`, find the `<AIChatSidebar ... />` component invocation around lines 150-163. Add the prop `conversationId` and assign it the value `selectedChat?.id`. This will pass the ID of the currently selected chat to the sidebar.
subtasks.testStrategy: After making the code change, run the application and open the React DevTools. Select the `AIChatSidebar` component and verify that the `conversationId` prop is present and holds the correct ID when a chat is selected in the UI.

subtasks.title: Add `leadId` Prop to AIChatSidebar Component
subtasks.description: In the same component instantiation, pass the `leadId` as a prop. This requires handling two possible locations for the lead ID within the `selectedChat` object.
subtasks.details: In `src/pages/ChatsPage.tsx`, at the same `<AIChatSidebar />` component, add the `leadId` prop. Set its value to `selectedChat?.lead_id || selectedChat?.leads?.id`. This expression ensures that the ID is correctly retrieved whether it's a direct property or nested within a `leads` object.
subtasks.testStrategy: Using React DevTools, inspect the `AIChatSidebar` component's props. Select different chats and confirm that the `leadId` prop is correctly populated based on the structure of the `selectedChat` data. Check both scenarios where `lead_id` is present and where `leads.id` is present.

subtasks.title: Update AIChatSidebar Prop-Types and Verify Data Reception
subtasks.description: Update the TypeScript interface for `AIChatSidebar`'s props to include the new `conversationId` and `leadId`, and then verify that the component receives these values at runtime.
subtasks.details: Navigate to the file where the `AIChatSidebar` component is defined. Find its props interface (e.g., `AIChatSidebarProps`) and add `conversationId?: string;` and `leadId?: string;`. This will resolve any TypeScript errors. As a temporary verification step, add `console.log({ conversationId, leadId })` inside the `AIChatSidebar` component's body to confirm in the browser console that the props are being received correctly when a chat is selected.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the TypeScript compiler or check your IDE for any type errors to ensure the prop types are correct. Then, run the application, open the developer console, navigate to the chats page, and select a conversation. Verify that the console log shows the expected `conversationId` and `leadId`.

tasks.title: Fix 2/3: Pass Tracking IDs to `generateAIResponse`
tasks.description: Ensure the `conversationId` and `leadId` are passed down to the AI response generation function to enable conversation tracking.
tasks.testStrategy: Set a breakpoint in the `generateAIResponse` function to confirm that `conversationId`, `leadId`, and `enableTracking` are received with the correct values when a message is sent.

subtasks.title: Update `AIChatSidebar` Props Interface and Destructure IDs
subtasks.description: Modify the props interface for the `AIChatSidebar` component to formally accept `conversationId` and `leadId`. Then, destructure these new props within the component's function signature to make them available in the component's scope.
subtasks.details: In `src/components/AIChatSidebar.tsx`, locate the props type definition (e.g., `AIChatSidebarProps`). Add `conversationId: string;` and `leadId: string;` to this type. Then, update the component's function definition to destructure `conversationId` and `leadId` from the props object.
subtasks.testStrategy: After making the changes, ensure the application compiles without any TypeScript errors. The component should still render correctly, although the new props won't be used yet.

subtasks.title: Modify `generateAIResponse` Function Call
subtasks.description: Update the arguments passed to the `generateAIResponse` function to include the tracking identifiers and enable the tracking flag.
subtasks.details: In `src/components/AIChatSidebar.tsx`, locate the `generateAIResponse` call around lines 81-86. Modify the object passed to this function to include the `conversationId` and `leadId` variables destructured in the previous step. Also, add the property `enableTracking: true` to the object.
subtasks.testStrategy: The code should compile successfully. The primary verification for this change will be performed in the next subtask by inspecting the network request.

subtasks.title: Verify Network Request Payload for Tracking IDs
subtasks.description: Run the application and use browser developer tools to confirm that the `conversationId` and `leadId` are correctly included in the payload of the network request initiated by `generateAIResponse`.
subtasks.details:
1. Run the application locally.
2. Open the browser's developer tools and navigate to the 'Network' tab.
3. In the application, interact with the AI Chat Sidebar to trigger a message generation.
4. Filter the network requests to find the API call made by `generateAIResponse` (e.g., a POST request to an endpoint like `/api/ai/response`).
5. Inspect the 'Payload' or 'Body' of this request to verify that `conversationId` and `leadId` are present and contain the expected values.
subtasks.testStrategy: The test is successful if the network request payload contains the `conversationId` and `leadId` keys with non-empty string values, confirming they are being passed correctly to the backend.

tasks.title: Fix 3/3: Use Dynamic `leadId` in `gemini.ts`
tasks.description: Correct the backend AI logic to use the passed `leadId` instead of a hardcoded empty string, completing the conversation tracking flow.
tasks.testStrategy: After sending a message in the UI, query the `conversation_memory` table in Supabase. Verify that a new record is created and the `lead_id` column is populated correctly.

subtasks.title: 1/3: Update the `generateContent` function signature to accept `leadId`
subtasks.description: Modify the function signature in `src/lib/gemini.ts` that handles content generation to accept an optional `leadId` string parameter. This is a prerequisite for passing the dynamic ID down to the database logic.
subtasks.details: Locate the function that contains the `conversation_memory` insertion logic (likely named `generateContent` or similar). Add `leadId?: string` to its list of parameters. This will cause TypeScript errors at the call sites, which will be fixed in a later subtask.
subtasks.testStrategy: After modifying the function signature, run the TypeScript compiler (`tsc` or through the IDE). Confirm that type errors appear where the function is called, as it now expects a new argument. This validates that the correct function was identified.

subtasks.title: 2/3: Replace hardcoded `leadId` with the dynamic parameter
subtasks.description: With the `leadId` now available within the function scope, replace the hardcoded empty string with the value from the new parameter when inserting a record into the `conversation_memory` table.
subtasks.details: Inside the modified function in `src/lib/gemini.ts`, find the database insertion call for `conversation_memory` (around line 216). Change the line `leadId: ''` to `leadId: leadId || ''`. This uses the passed `leadId` if it exists, otherwise defaulting to an empty string to prevent errors.
subtasks.testStrategy: Perform a code review to ensure the change from `''` to `leadId || ''` is correctly implemented. If unit tests exist for this function, update them to pass a mock `leadId` and assert that the database insertion logic is called with the correct dynamic value.

subtasks.title: 3/3: Update API route handler to pass `leadId` to `generateContent`
subtasks.description: Complete the data flow by finding where the `generateContent` function is called (likely in an API route) and passing the `leadId` from the incoming request. This resolves the type errors from the first subtask.
subtasks.details: Navigate to the API route file that calls the function modified in `gemini.ts` (e.g., `src/app/api/chat/route.ts`). In the request handler (e.g., `POST`), extract the `leadId` from the request body. Then, pass this `leadId` as an argument when you call the `generateContent` function.
subtasks.testStrategy: Conduct an end-to-end test. Use an API client like Postman to send a request to the chat API endpoint, including a `leadId` in the JSON body. After the request completes, query your database to verify that the new entry in the `conversation_memory` table contains the `leadId` you sent.

tasks.title: Install TanStack Virtual for Chat Virtualization
tasks.description: Install and configure TanStack Virtual to prepare for implementing virtual scrolling in the chat interface, preventing browser crashes with long conversations.
tasks.details:
Install the necessary package using npm or your preferred package manager.

```bash
npm install @tanstack/react-virtual
```
No code changes are required in this step, only installation. This sets the stage for the implementation task.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the package `@tanstack/react-virtual` is listed in `package.json` and the `node_modules` directory. Ensure the application still builds and runs without errors.

tasks.title: Implement Chat Message Virtualization
tasks.description: Implement virtual scrolling in the chat message list using TanStack Virtual to ensure high performance even with thousands of messages.
tasks.details: In `src/components/Chat/ChatInterface.tsx`, refactor the message list rendering. Use the `useVirtualizer` hook from `@tanstack/react-virtual`. The implementation should wrap the messages in a scrollable container, use the virtualizer to get the list of virtual items, and render only those items, applying the correct styles for positioning.
tasks.testStrategy: Load a conversation with over 1000 messages. Confirm that the UI remains responsive and scrolling is smooth. Use browser developer tools to inspect the DOM and verify that only a small subset of message elements are rendered at any time.

tasks.title: Implement Database-Level Pagination for Leads & Templates
tasks.description: Refactor the `useLeads` and `useTemplates` hooks to fetch data in pages instead of all at once, improving initial load time and reducing memory usage.
tasks.details: Modify `src/hooks/useLeads.ts` and `src/hooks/useTemplates.ts`. Change the Supabase query to use `.range(from, to)` to fetch a limited number of records (e.g., 50). Implement a `loadMore` function that fetches the next page of data and appends it to the existing state. Use cursor-based pagination for optimal performance by tracking the last fetched item's ID or timestamp.
tasks.testStrategy: Use the browser's network tab to verify that the initial fetch only requests a limited number of items. Click the 'Load More' button and confirm a new network request is made for the next page. The UI should update to show the new items.

tasks.title: DB Schema 1/3: Add Foreign Key Constraints
tasks.description: Create a new Supabase migration file to add foreign key constraints to the database, ensuring data integrity between leads, conversations, and messages.
tasks.details:
Create a new SQL migration file in your Supabase project. Add the following SQL statements to enforce relationships:

```sql
-- Add foreign key constraints
ALTER TABLE conversations ADD CONSTRAINT fk_lead FOREIGN KEY (lead_id) REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
ALTER TABLE messages ADD CONSTRAINT fk_conversation FOREIGN KEY (conversation_id) REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
```
Adding `ON DELETE CASCADE` is a good practice to clean up related data automatically.
tasks.testStrategy: Apply the migration. Attempt to insert a `message` with a non-existent `conversation_id`. The database should reject the insertion with a foreign key violation error. Verify that deleting a `lead` also deletes its associated `conversations`.

tasks.title: DB Schema 2/3: Add Performance Indexes
tasks.description: Add indexes to frequently queried columns in the database to significantly improve query performance for fetching messages, conversations, and leads.
tasks.testStrategy: Before and after applying the migration, run an `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a query fetching messages for a conversation (e.g., `SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = 'some-id'`). The 'after' query plan should show the use of the new index and have a lower execution cost.

tasks.title: DB Schema 3/3: Enable Basic Row Level Security
tasks.description: Enable Row Level Security (RLS) on key tables and create basic policies. As this is a personal tool, the policies will be permissive but establish the security foundation.
tasks.testStrategy: After applying the migration, verify that all data fetching and modification operations in the application continue to work as expected. The permissive `USING (true)` clause should not block any legitimate operations.

tasks.title: Setup Testing Framework (Vitest + RTL)
tasks.description: Install and configure Vitest and React Testing Library to establish a modern, fast, and effective unit and component testing environment.
tasks.details:
Run the following command to install the development dependencies:

```bash
npm install -D vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jsdom @vitejs/plugin-react
```
Create a `vitest.config.ts` file at the project root to configure the testing environment, including setting up `jsdom` and global imports.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a simple test file (e.g., `src/components/ui/Button.test.tsx`) with a basic test that renders a component and asserts its content. Run `npm test` (or `npx vitest`) and confirm that the test passes.

tasks.title: Write Unit Tests for Core AI Functions
tasks.description: Write unit tests for the core AI logic in `gemini.ts` to ensure its functions behave as expected and to prevent regressions.
tasks.details: Create a test file `src/lib/gemini.test.ts`. Mock the external Gemini API dependency. Write test cases for the `generateAIResponse` function. Test different scenarios: with and without tracking enabled, with different contexts, and ensure it formats the request payload correctly.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the tests via Vitest. The test suite should achieve high coverage for `gemini.ts`. All tests should pass, confirming the logic for payload construction and function invocation is correct under various conditions.

tasks.title: Write Integration Tests for Data Hooks
tasks.description: Write integration tests for the custom data fetching hooks (`useLeads`, `useTemplates`) to validate their interaction with the Supabase backend.
tasks.details: Create test files like `src/hooks/useLeads.test.ts`. Use Vitest to test the hooks. You may need to mock the Supabase client to simulate API responses for pagination. Test the initial fetch, the `loadMore` functionality, and loading/error states.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the tests. Verify that the hooks correctly manage state (data, loading, error) based on the mocked Supabase responses. Ensure the pagination logic correctly appends data.

tasks.title: Setup E2E Testing with Playwright
tasks.description: Install and configure Playwright to enable end-to-end testing for critical user workflows, ensuring the application works as a whole.
tasks.details:
Initialize Playwright in the project by running:

```bash
npm init playwright@latest
```
Follow the prompts to configure the project. This will create a `playwright.config.ts` file, an example test, and a `tests` directory. Adjust the config's `webServer` command to start your local development server before tests run.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the example test provided by the Playwright installer (`npx playwright test`). It should launch a browser, navigate to the specified URL, and pass successfully.

tasks.title: Create E2E Test for Core Conversation Workflow
tasks.description: Create an E2E test script that simulates a user creating a lead, starting a conversation, and receiving an AI-assisted response.
tasks.details:
Create a new test file in the Playwright `tests` directory. The script should:
1. Navigate to the leads page.
2. Click a 'Create Lead' button and fill out the form.
3. Navigate to the new lead's chat page.
4. Type and send a message.
5. Wait for the AI response to appear and assert its presence.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the new E2E test. The test should pass, visually confirming in the test runner's browser that the entire workflow from lead creation to AI response is functioning correctly.

tasks.title: Split AppContext 1/4: Create UIContext
tasks.description: Create a new, dedicated `UIContext` to manage UI-specific state like theme (dark/light mode), sidebar visibility, etc., to begin splitting the monolithic `AppContext`.
tasks.details: Create a new file `src/contexts/UIContext.tsx`. Define the context shape, create the provider component, and a custom hook `useUI` for easy consumption. Move any UI-related state and functions from `AppContext.tsx` into this new context.
tasks.testStrategy: Wrap the application with the new `UIProvider`. Refactor a component that uses UI state (e.g., a theme toggle button) to use the `useUI` hook. Verify that the functionality (e.g., toggling dark mode) still works correctly.

tasks.title: Split AppContext 2/4: Create LeadsContext
tasks.description: Create a new `LeadsContext` to handle all state and logic related to lead management, including fetching, creating, and updating leads.
tasks.details: Create `src/contexts/LeadsContext.tsx`. Move all lead-related state, the `useLeads` hook logic, and any related functions from `AppContext` into this new provider. Create a `useLeadsContext` hook for components to access this state.
tasks.testStrategy: Replace direct `AppContext` usage in lead-related components (e.g., `LeadsPage`) with the new `useLeadsContext` hook. Verify that leads are still fetched, displayed, and can be interacted with as before.

tasks.title: Split AppContext 3/4: Create TemplatesContext
tasks.description: Create a `TemplatesContext` to manage message templates, separating this concern from the main application context.
tasks.details: Create `src/contexts/TemplatesContext.tsx`. Move all state and logic for fetching and managing templates from `AppContext` into this new provider. Expose the state and functions through a `useTemplatesContext` hook.
tasks.testStrategy: Refactor components that use templates to get data from `useTemplatesContext`. Verify that templates are loaded and can be selected and used in the chat interface.

tasks.title: Split AppContext 4/4: Create ChatContext
tasks.description: Create a `ChatContext` to manage the state of the active chat session, including messages, conversation ID, and AI interaction state.
tasks.details: Create `src/contexts/ChatContext.tsx`. This context will hold the state for the currently selected conversation, its messages, loading states for AI responses, etc. Move this logic from `AppContext` and page-level state into the new provider. Create a `useChatContext` hook.
tasks.testStrategy: Wrap the main chat view with the `ChatProvider`. Refactor `ChatInterface.tsx` and `AIChatSidebar.tsx` to use `useChatContext`. Verify that sending and receiving messages, and all chat-related UI updates, work correctly.

tasks.title: Finalize Context Split and Deprecate AppContext
tasks.description: Complete the context refactoring by removing the now-delegated state from `AppContext`, leaving it as a lightweight container or removing it entirely if no longer needed.
tasks.details: Go back to `src/contexts/AppContext.tsx`. Remove all the state and logic that was migrated to the domain-specific contexts. The `AppProvider` should now compose the new providers (`UIProvider`, `LeadsProvider`, etc.). Update the main application entry point (`App.tsx` or `main.tsx`) to use this new provider structure.
tasks.testStrategy: Perform a full regression test of the application. All major features (viewing leads, chatting, using templates, changing themes) should work. Use React DevTools to confirm that re-renders are now more localized (e.g., typing in the chat input should not re-render the leads list).

tasks.title: Implement React Router for Navigation
tasks.description: Integrate React Router to manage navigation, providing URL-based routing, browser history support, and a foundation for future features like route guards.
tasks.details:
Install the library:

```bash
npm install react-router-dom
```
Refactor `App.tsx` to use `createBrowserRouter` and `RouterProvider`. Define routes for the main pages (e.g., `/`, `/chats/:id`, `/leads`). Replace programmatic navigation with `<Link>` components or the `useNavigate` hook.
tasks.testStrategy: Navigate through the app using the new routes. Verify that the URL in the browser updates correctly. Test the browser's back and forward buttons; they should navigate through the app's history. Bookmark a specific chat URL, close the tab, and reopen it; it should load the correct chat.

tasks.title: Implement Lazy Loading for Routes
tasks.description: Implement lazy loading for routes using React.lazy() and Suspense to improve initial page load performance by code-splitting page components.
tasks.testStrategy: Open the browser's network tab. Clear the cache and reload the page. On initial load, only the code for the main page should be downloaded. When you navigate to another page (e.g., a chat), verify that a new JavaScript chunk for that page is downloaded on demand.

tasks.title: Refactor AI Prompt Engine for Dynamic Construction
tasks.description: Refactor the AI prompt generation logic to be dynamic and phase-aware, constructing prompts based on the current state of the conversation.
tasks.details: Create a new module `src/lib/prompt-manager.ts`. This module will export a function, e.g., `constructPrompt(phase, context, history)`. This function will use a switch statement or a map to select a base prompt template based on the `phase` (e.g., 'introduction', 'qualification', 'booking'). It will then inject the relevant `context` (lead info, templates) and a summary of the `history`.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for `prompt-manager.ts`. For each conversation phase, provide sample inputs and assert that the generated prompt string is correctly constructed and contains the expected information. The tests should cover all phases defined in the prompt engineering analysis document.

tasks.title: Implement AI Response Validation and Scoring
tasks.description: Implement a system for validating and scoring AI responses to ensure they are relevant and high-quality before being displayed or used.
tasks.details: Create `src/lib/response-validator.ts`. This module will have a function `validateResponse(response, context)` that returns a score from 0.0 to 1.0. The validation can check for key phrases, appropriate sentiment, or whether it answers a user's question. Initially, this can be rule-based. The score can be used for logging and future A/B testing.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the `validateResponse` function. Provide it with various sample AI responses (good, bad, irrelevant) and assert that it returns an appropriate score for each.

tasks.title: Implement Few-Shot Example Injection in Prompt Engine
tasks.description: Enhance the prompt engine to dynamically inject few-shot examples into the prompt, guiding the AI to produce better-formatted and more contextually appropriate responses.
tasks.details: In `src/lib/prompt-manager.ts`, create a repository of few-shot examples categorized by conversation phase. When constructing a prompt, select 2-3 relevant examples (input/output pairs) and prepend them to the main prompt. The selection should be based on the current conversation phase.
tasks.testStrategy: In the unit tests for the prompt manager, verify that for a given phase, the correct few-shot examples are included in the final prompt string. Manually trigger AI responses in the app and observe if the output quality and format improve.

tasks.title: Apply DRY Principle and Consolidate Utilities (Task 6)
tasks.description: Perform a codebase-wide review to identify and eliminate duplicated code, creating shared utilities and hooks to improve maintainability (DRY principle).
tasks.details: Audit the codebase, especially within components and hooks. Look for repeated logic (e.g., data formatting, API call patterns). Extract this logic into new reusable functions in `src/utils/` or custom hooks in `src/hooks/`. Refactor the original code to use these new shared modules.
tasks.testStrategy: After refactoring, run all existing unit, integration, and E2E tests. They should all continue to pass. Manually test the refactored parts of the application to ensure no behavior has changed. Code review should confirm a reduction in lines of code and duplication.

tasks.title: Refactor Monolithic Components (Task 7)
tasks.description: Break down large, monolithic components into smaller, single-responsibility components and reusable UI primitives to improve readability and reusability.
tasks.details: Identify large components (e.g., `ChatInterface`, `AIChatSidebar`). Break them down into smaller, more focused components. For example, `ChatInterface` could be split into `MessageList`, `MessageInput`, and `ChatHeader`. Generic UI elements like buttons and inputs should be moved to `src/components/ui/`.
tasks.testStrategy: Use Storybook or a similar tool to render and test the new primitive components in isolation. For the refactored feature components, rely on existing component and E2E tests to ensure that the UI and functionality remain unchanged after the refactor.

tasks.title: Implement Memoization Optimizations (Task 9)
tasks.description: Apply performance optimization techniques like memoization across the application to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
tasks.details: Wrap components that render frequently with `React.memo`. Use the `useMemo` hook for expensive calculations and `useCallback` for functions passed as props to memoized children. Profile the application with React DevTools to identify key areas for optimization.
tasks.testStrategy: Use the React DevTools Profiler to record interactions before and after the changes. The 'after' profile should show fewer component re-renders for the same interactions (e.g., typing in an input field).

tasks.title: Optimize Database Queries (Task 10)
tasks.description: Analyze and optimize database queries to ensure they are efficient and meet the performance target of < 200ms.
tasks.details: Review all Supabase queries in the codebase. Use `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` in the Supabase SQL Editor for slow queries to understand their execution plans. Ensure all queries that filter on common columns (like `conversation_id`, `lead_id`, `status`) are using the indexes created in a previous task. Refactor queries as needed.
tasks.testStrategy: Measure the execution time of key queries using the browser's network tab or directly in Supabase. All primary data-fetching queries should consistently execute in under 200ms with a representative amount of data.

tasks.title: Analyze and Optimize Bundle Size
tasks.description: Analyze the application's bundle size and implement strategies to reduce it, such as tree-shaking and optimizing dependencies.
tasks.details: Install `webpack-bundle-analyzer` or a similar tool for Vite (e.g., `rollup-plugin-visualizer`). Generate a bundle analysis report. Identify large dependencies that could be replaced with smaller alternatives or that are not being properly tree-shaken. Ensure libraries with side effects are handled correctly.
tasks.testStrategy: Generate a bundle report before and after optimizations. The 'after' report should show a noticeable reduction in the overall bundle size, particularly for the main entry chunk. Verify the application still functions correctly after dependency changes.

tasks.title: Implement Script Template Engine (Task 21)
tasks.description: Implement a dynamic script template engine that allows for variable interpolation based on lead data, enabling personalized messaging.
tasks.details: Create a `src/lib/template-engine.ts`. The engine should take a template string (e.g., 'Hi {{lead.name}}, are you free on Tuesday?') and a lead object. It should replace placeholders like `{{lead.name}}` with the actual data from the lead object. This will be used to customize messages before sending.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for the template engine. Test it with various templates and lead data objects. Cover edge cases like missing data, nested properties, and multiple variables in one template. Ensure it correctly interpolates all variables.
